title: Derived pushforward commutes canonically with strict tower inverse limit
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi on small sites, with structural ring map $f^{-1}S\to R$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and K-injective total derived direct image [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For $T=R,S$ put $\operatorname{Tow}(T)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(T))$, the category of strict inverse sequences with levelwise exactness. Let $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ apply module direct image levelwise and let $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ be its total right derived functor. Write $L_R,L_S$ for total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))$, there are natural evaluation identifications $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M\cong Rf_*\operatorname{ev}_nM$ and a canonical natural isomorphism
$$a_{f,M}:Rf_*L_R(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_S(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M).$$
The comparison is the one induced by the equality of underived composite direct images $f_*\lim_R=\lim_S f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$: regard inverse limit as direct image from the tower ringed topos and compare both derived composites with the total derived functor of that common direct image. Under the evaluation identifications, it commutes with all tower projections. No boundedness, constructibility, exact countable products, or identification $f^{-1}S=R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the four total right derived functors using K-injective resolutions. The strict tower category is Grothendieck abelian, after transporting the small-diagram theorem across the universe-lift equivalence. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence; every additive functor preserves these. Thus the K-injective localizer derives each complex functor followed by Q, and the canonical totalRightDerived units are isomorphisms on K-injectives.

Evaluation detects tower quasi-isomorphisms, so localization gives evaluation into strict towers of derived objects. Exact evaluation preserves K-injectives. Compare the two right derived functors into that tower category by the universal property to construct e, with its unit normalization on every complex. The same universal property applied to each strict limit projection constructs pR and pS and their equations.

Forgetful functors from module sheaves to underlying sheaves preserve limits and reflect isomorphisms. The underlying topos direct image is a right adjoint. Its limit preservation and the supplied underlying natural isomorphism imply that module direct image preserves tower limits. Set c to preservesLimitNatIso, whose hom is limit.post. The constant-tower functor is exact and left adjoint to inverse limit, so inverse limit preserves K-injectives.

For a K-injective source tower I, resolve its levelwise pushforward by a K-injective tower j:f_*I→T. Inverse-limit acyclicity makes lim(j) a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality and the invertibility of the inverse-limit derived unit on T imply that this unit is also invertible on f_*I. Consequently both composite units are right derived units for the respective underived composites. Apply rightDerivedNatIso to c on complexes followed by Q. The defining equation of rightDerivedNatTrans gives the exact normalization of a.

Apply rightDerived_ext to the two projection maps from the composite derived functor. On a complex X, postcompose with Rf of the invertible identification εR. Substitute the normalization of a, use naturality of pS, apply the normalization of e, and then apply the pS equation. Degreewise, preservesLimitIso_hom_π says that c followed by the target projection equals pushforward of the source projection. Naturality of ηf and the pR equation finish the equality. Cancellation and right derived uniqueness give the equation on every derived object.
